name: Inter 2020/21 (Antonio Conte)
scopeNote: Inter under Antonio Conte, 2020/21 Serie A title season only. First match 26 Sep 2020 (4-3 v Fiorentina, season opener per Goal 2020-09-27); last match 23 May 2021 v Udinese (Calciomercato 2021-05-23: Conte speaks after the Udinese match). Conte left in May 2021 (26 May, from Sky Sport URL date, not read). Sources call the shape 3-5-2 (also 3-1-4-2 / 3-4-1-2 with Eriksen or Barella as a 10 early in the season, Serpents of Madonnina); defends in a 5-3-2 mid-block (Coaches' Voice). Not zonal-pressing/possession football: Inter averaged 45% possession in the winning run and were a counter-attacking side. Exact first/last match dates are from memory plus one source each; a second source was not found. The Cult of Calcio piece 'Inter vs Juventus: more threatening from open play' is 2021/22 (Inzaghi, Dzeko) and was excluded.
openQuestions: Man vs zonal marking: no in-period source states it. Cult of Calcio's 'tight man-to-man marking in certain zones' is from the 2021/22 Inzaghi article and was excluded; Coaches' Voice describes pressing traps and zonal-looking shifts without naming a marking scheme.
Coaches' Voice overview (2023) covers Conte's Inter 2019-21 together; items tagged 2019/20-2020/21 may partly describe the first season.
Squad age: no source gives an average; only signings (Vidal 33, Kolarov 34, Young 35) from 90min / Wikipedia-style data. Veterans were used alongside Barella (23), Bastoni, Hakimi (21).
Conte's departure date (26 May 2021) and the 23 May Udinese final-day date rest on one source each; Sky Sport pages (storia tattica, Zanetti, Conte parole) were unreadable.
Early Champions League exit: only Serpents of Madonnina (tier C) verified; Conte's own post-exit statements not read.
Conte's pre-season near-resignation (summer 2020) predates the first match and is not counted.

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: That approach evolved during 2020/21 (above). While one of their front two – most consistently Lukaku – continued to move short, retain the ball and link with those making runs, their wing-backs made penetrative runs through the centre of the pitch.

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: By running into different positions, Inter's wing-backs could deliver crosses from new angles and therefore increase the variety they offered

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: At Inter, the 5-3-2 they often defended with (above) sometimes became a 5-2-3 in which one striker worked to limit access into the opposing single pivot while the other striker and an attacking midfielder pressed the opposition's central defenders.

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: for brief periods, Inter therefore pressed with a 4-4-2 (above). From this shape, they worked to keep the ball to one side of the pitch, and their front two stopped passes into the centre of the pitch before pressing their opposing central defenders and goalkeeper.

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: When they were defending with a mid or lower block, their central midfielders worked to provide defensive support in wide areas; the closest striker screened access back infield; and their wing-backs attempted to force play wide.

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: In the same way their wing-backs' movements enhanced their attacking potential, they also made Inter's defence more resilient. Their back three and defensive midfielder received greater support because their attacking midfielders' positioning meant that they were considerably less exposed

sources.title: Antonio Conte: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: The versatility of Romelu Lukaku and Lautaro Martínez also proved a strength. Both are capable of holding the ball up or running in behind, and therefore complement each other when operating on different lines.

confidence.reason: Several tier A-B sources (Coaches' Voice, TFA, Cult of Calcio, GFNI) agree on shape, wing-back and transition play for 2020/21, but marking scheme is unsourced, set pieces and squad age thin, and many items are tier C.
